title: Introduce hierarchical row-tiling and smart header snap for hybrid virtual tables
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: Our current virtual table struggles with very wide datasets where users need to scan groups of rows semantically (e.g., multi-row results per entity). Existing collapse/pinning patterns focus on columns; row-level grouping and header behavior are inconsistent across density modes and cause cognitive load when items reflow during virtualization.

Goal: Ship a design pattern and component spec that enables hierarchical row-tiling (soft groups that tile multiple logical rows into a single visual unit at higher densities) combined with a smart header 'snap' that anchors group headers while scrolling. This should improve scanability on narrow and dense surfaces, play nicely with keyboard navigation and screen readers, and be implementable within our virtualized renderer with minimal perf overhead.

Outcomes: A high-fidelity component spec, token mapping for density, interaction rules (hover/focus/selection), and a lightweight prototype to validate perf trade-offs with engineering.

Scope exclusions: This ticket covers presentation and interaction patterns only. Row grouping heuristics for backend aggregation and server-side annotation are out of scope and will be captured as a dependency if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec includes: visual states (expanded / tiled / collapsed), density token mapping (compact / cozy / comfortable), and header snap rules for desktop and mobile
Prototype demonstrates tiled row rendering in the virtual list without causing jank on a 2k-item dataset (engineering smoke test)
Keyboard navigation: group-level focus, expand/collapse via Space/Enter, and arrow key behavior documented
Accessibility: ARIA pattern documented for grouped rows and header snapshots; WCAG 2.1 AA considerations listed
Edge cases documented: mixed-height children, row-selection semantics, and interaction with column-resize and frozen columns
design_notes: Introduce 'tile unit' token that defines the visual footprint for grouped rows at each density
Header snap should be configurable: persistent (stays pinned for the group range) vs contextual (appears while group is in view)
Visual affordance for tiled rows: a subtle divider + stacked preview for overflowed cells to hint more content
Consider 'shelf header' microcopy to surface group counts and concise filters (e.g., '3 matches')
Animation: prefer opacity+translate over scale to avoid layout thrashing in virtualized containers
decisions: Use a CSS transform-based approach for header snap to avoid reflow; engineers to attempt using translateY on a fixed overlay
Default to always-on tiled preview in compact density, toggleable in user prefs for comfortable density
Expose an API flag (rowTiling: 'auto' | 'off' | 'on') for early engineering rollout and A/B testing
Defer server-side grouping; frontend will detect adjacency heuristics (same entity-id or group key) for initial prototype
comments: 2025-01-09 - Ethan Cole: Reviewed initial sketches. Concern: virtualizer needs to know the tile height in advance. Suggest adding a predictable token for tile height. --assigned to engineering to evaluate feasibility.

2025-01-15 - Priya Nair: Usability study plan added. 6 participants (B2B data analysts). Test goals: find vs. scan tasks comparing tiled vs. dense single rows. Link to script: https://docs.redwood.ai/ux/table-tiling-usability.md
2025-01-22 - Maya Alvarez (PM): Noted potential conflict with upcoming frozen-column work. Added ENG-21014 as dependency to ensure tiled headers don't overlap pinned columns.

2025-01-28 - Ethan Cole: Spike complete. Prototype uses fixed overlay for header snap and measures no perceivable jank on desktop Chrome for 5k rows when tileHeight token is used. Spike notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/spikes/tree/main/row-tiling

2025-02-05 - Accessibility review (Tom Harris): Recommend ARIA roletype treegrid with group row roles and explicit aria-expanded attributes. Also flagged screen reader announcement order; will follow up with examples in spec.

2025-02-12 - Priya Nair: Iterated visuals based on research: changed preview affordance from stacked cards to truncated inline peek to reduce noise. Updated Figma. Ready for design handoff on 2025-02-18.
